items.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: that was through the help of Phil Carroll who runs the Atlanta jazz party. He knew that I had not been recorded that much and so what he did was set up a recording session

ctx.x: Yeah. He came in there a couple of times and I figured he would ask me to record for him and never did. And that probably was, it didn’t leave me feeling too good about it. The one who has recorded what I’ve done again is the traditional Jazzology, George Buck in New Orleans, but that was through the help of Phil Carroll who runs the Atlanta jazz party. He knew that I had not been recorded that much and so what he did was set up a recording session after one or, actually four or five of these Atlanta jazz…
Is that what this came from? The CD?
